sources.entry: Format inspired by the GPU-side list at wafer-ai/gpu-perf-engineering-resources.

summary.one_liner: A curated, link-based reading list for learning GPU performance engineering and LLM inference, ordered from single-request inference through GPU kernels, inference engines, and distributed serving.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome"-style list of resources rather than software. It is organized into six numbered sections: GPU fundamentals, kernel optimization (including matmul, tensor cores, and attention), programming models and profiling (Triton, CUTLASS/CuTe, ROCm, JAX Pallas, NKI), inference engines (continuous batching, KV cache, quantization, speculative decoding, structured decoding), distributed inference (parallelism, MoE serving, prefill/decode disaggregation, serving benchmarks), and current hardware (NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, AWS Trainium). A "Start here" section gives an ordered reading path, and a "Frontier" section covers AI-generated kernels and a watchlist of unproven hardware. The README states a source policy favoring original papers, specifications, creator repositories, and reproducible implementer reports, and says performance claims without hardware, workload, precision, baseline, and correctness details are omitted.
use_cases: Learning GPU programming and CUDA kernel optimization
Finding papers on FlashAttention, PagedAttention, and speculative decoding
Studying LLM inference serving and KV cache design
Reviewing quantization methods such as GPTQ, AWQ, and FP8/FP4 formats
Planning a reading path into AI performance engineering
Comparing GPU, TPU, and Trainium hardware documentation
notable: Ordered "Start here" reading path from inference basics to roofline modeling and serving SLOs
Source policy restricting core entries to originating papers, official specs, creator repos, or reproducible implementer reports
Covers NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, and AWS Trainium hardware stacks in one list
Separate Frontier section with a dated verification note and a watchlist of unproven hardware and techniques
caveats: Link list only; it contains no runnable code or installable tool
The Frontier section is explicitly marked as fast-changing evidence, and the README gives a verification date of 2026-10-17
Contribution rules are delegated to a CONTRIBUTING.md file not included in the README
